newsitem.title: USA: Burmese gov't-in-exile files suit against Unocal.
newsitem.headline: Burmese gov't-in-exile files suit against Unocal.

text.p: A self-described Burmese government-in-exile filed a suit in U.S. federal court on Tuesday against Unocal Corp., a partner in the largest foreign investment project in the South Asian nation.

It charged the Los Angeles-based oil company with human rights violations in the venture, a $1.2 billion gas pipeline it owns with France's Total oil group, Burma's state-owned Myanmar Oil & Gas Enterprise and Thailand's PTT.
It accused the joint venture of using forced labor of tens of thousands of villagers, systematic destruction of villages in the pipeline region and other human rights atrocities.

"We are seeking an injunction against Unocal and monetary damages, which as you can imagine are enormous," said attorney Jason Atkins of Boston, Massachusetts-based Cristobal Bonifaz, representing the National Coalition Government of the Union of Burma (NCGUB) and Federation of Trade Unions of Burma (FTUB).
Total and Unocal have been targets of international activist groups protesting the Burmese military government's human rights record and crackdown on democracy campaigners.
Unocal was not immediately available for comment.

The NCGUB has its principal offices in Washington. The Federation of Trade Unions of Burma is based in Bangkok, Thailand. The two groups have filed the lawsuit on their own behalf and on behalf of the citizens of Burma.

The suit seeks a court order halting Unocal's role in the joint venture, which is building a natural gas pipeline into Thailand. It alleges that Unocal relies on the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) -- the Burmese military regime -- for providing and maintaining all military operations in the pipeline region, severely repressing Burmese citizens.

SLORC seized power in Burma in 1988 and has repressed the National League for Democracy (NLD) since 1990 with thousands of arrests. The lawyers said the NLD, headed by Aung San Suu Kyi, has met secretly and designated a group of elected representatives to form a government-in-exile.
